text: The book concludes that Physarum's anticipatory slowing in the cold-shock experiments definitively proves it stores a discrete, representational memory of the stimulus, exactly as a neuron would.
explanation: False. The book presents the finding as contested and better explained by entrainment of an internal oscillation than by any discrete, representational storage; Physarum has no synapses or synaptic plasticity. The behavioral observation (slowing at the trained period) is robust, but the strong 'representational memory' interpretation is explicitly not established.
